transcript: Today I will talk about climate change. The main cause is the burning of fossil fuels like coal, oil and gas, which releases carbon dioxide. Carbon dioxide is a greenhouse gas, so it traps heat and the average temperature of the planet goes up. Because of this, glaciers and ice sheets are melting and sea levels are rising, which is dangerous for coastal cities. We also see more heatwaves, droughts and floods. To reduce emissions we need renewable energy like solar and wind power, and governments must work together, for example through the Paris Agreement.

My topic is climate change and I want to focus on one part of it, which is the oceans. When the planet warms, the ice in Greenland and Antarctica melts and the water goes into the sea. Water also expands when it gets warmer. So the sea level rises and places near the coast and small islands can be flooded. Warm water is also bad for coral reefs, because corals become white and can die. That is why protecting the oceans matters.

The earth is getting hotter, and we humans are mostly responsible. Every time we run power stations on coal or drive petrol cars, we put gases into the air that act like a blanket around the planet. Cutting down jungles removes the trees that would soak up those gases. The results are frozen regions turning to water, oceans creeping onto the land, and summers that are scorching. Switching to sunlight and wind for our electricity, and making our homes waste less power, is the way forward.

I want to start with something from my own life. Last summer my city had a heatwave and the temperature stayed above forty degrees for days. My grandmother could not go outside and our electricity kept failing. Scientists say heatwaves like this are becoming more common because of climate change, which is caused mainly by burning fossil fuels. After that summer my family started using the bus more and we switched off lights we did not need. These are small steps, but if many people do them, together with clean energy from governments, they make a difference.

Today I want to talk about my favourite sport, which is cricket. I started playing when I was eight years old with my cousins in the street. Cricket teaches you patience, because a test match can last five days. My favourite player is a fast bowler who can bowl at more than one hundred and forty kilometres per hour. Last month our college team won the inter-college tournament and I scored my first half century. I think every student should play a sport because it keeps you fit and helps you make friends.

Climate change is caused mainly by burning fossil fuels, which releases carbon dioxide. Many cities are now building metro rail systems so that fewer people need cars. Some companies are also testing machines that capture carbon dioxide directly from the air. Under the Paris Agreement, countries agreed to keep warming below four degrees Celsius. Planting trees is good because forests store carbon.

Sleep is very important for students. While we sleep, the brain is still working and it strengthens the memories we made during the day, moving them into long-term memory. That is why studying and then sleeping works better than staying up all night. When we do not sleep enough, it is hard to concentrate the next day and we make more mistakes. Teenagers need about eight to ten hours. To sleep better, we should go to bed at the same time every day, put our phones away and avoid coffee in the evening.

I want to talk about how to sleep better. First, keep a regular schedule and wake up at the same time even on weekends. Second, stop using your phone before bed, because the blue light keeps you awake. Third, do not drink coffee or energy drinks in the evening. Finally, keep your room dark and quiet. These simple habits can really improve the quality of your sleep.

I would like to share my recipe for vegetable biryani. First you soak the rice for half an hour. Then you fry onions until they are golden and add tomatoes, ginger, garlic and spices. Add the vegetables and cook them for ten minutes. Layer the rice on top, add saffron milk and cook on low heat until the rice is soft. Serve it with raita and enjoy it with your family.

Today I want to explain how sleep affects studying. Sleep helps us store the new memories we make during the day. However, teenagers only need about four hours of sleep each night, so there is no reason to sleep longer. Staying awake all night before an exam is the best way to remember everything. Some students use a mobile application that tracks their sleep cycles and wakes them up gently. Drinking coffee late in the evening can make it harder to fall asleep. Good sleep also helps the body fight illness and keeps us healthy.
